title: Relative Frobenius norms and density-one ordinary reduction
summary: The full Newton polygon and a density-one p-rank lower bound in adjoint type A1, exact original-field ordinary densities in a tensor case and for balanced imaginary quadratic fourfolds, and sharp limits on local relative-norm bounds.
abstract: For an abelian variety of adjoint Mumford--Tate type \(A_1\) over a number field, we prove that after finite extension its Newton slopes belong to \(\{0,1/2,1\}\) and its \(p\)-rank exceeds half its dimension at a set of primes of natural density one. We express the half-slope multiplicity in terms of the adjoint factors on which Frobenius has flat Newton slopes. A weighted bound on these factors gives density-one ordinary reduction when the Hodge cocharacter is nontrivial on at most two geometric factors above each rational simple adjoint factor. In a tensor case with at most two active embeddings, we identify the least extension giving density one and compute the ordinary density over the original field. For an abelian fourfold of signature \((2,2)\) whose full geometric rational endomorphism algebra is imaginary quadratic, ordinary reduction has natural density one over the original field. On components that exchange the coefficient embeddings, the parity comes from a Pfaffian, with a sharp finite-field bound in higher even rank. For a Rosati-compatible CM field action with a mixed Hodge pair we also bound all intermediate relative Frobenius coefficient norms simultaneously, giving a closed formula for the sharp numerical minimum \(p\)-rank of split polygons.
next_steps: External specialist review of the original-field tensor descent, the adjoint p-rank formula, and the Pfaffian argument.
Investigate ordinary reduction at completely split primes with three independent Hodge-active labels.
